business_problem: Kredivo needed a more centralized, lower-latency streaming platform so it could scale credit and analytics pipelines, detect fraud and production issues faster, and avoid building a dedicated infrastructure team just to run Kafka.
solution_summary: Kredivo adopted Confluent Cloud as the streaming layer inside its microservice-based financial platform so it could centralize data movement without overhauling its cloud strategy. The company streams customer and loan-application data through the managed backbone, migrated from AWS to GCP, and uses a sink connector to land databases in BigQuery for analytics and warehouse use cases. That same real-time foundation powers creditworthiness decisions, fraud and payment-error alerts, and marketing campaign dashboards that depend on fresher data than the company's previous setup could provide. Because Confluent productized the Kafka and connector model Kredivo wanted, the team gained easier monitoring, better security and disaster recovery options, and a much faster way to spin up new pipelines for finance, marketing, and risk teams without staffing a dedicated operations group.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Runs the centralized streaming platform for customer, loan, and analytics data across Kredivo's microservice architecture.

solution_components.name: sink connector
solution_components.role: Streams Kredivo's databases into BigQuery after the move from AWS to GCP.

solution_components.name: Google BigQuery
